shortDescription: Li-S Energy ASX:LIS has completed the first commercial sale of its Australian-made lithium-sulphur battery cells, with 10Ah Power Cells shipped for evaluation by US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) across crewed and uncrewed systems in air, land, and maritime domains.The cells were purchased by…

children: has completed the first commercial sale of its Australian-made lithium-sulphur battery cells, with 10Ah Power Cells shipped for evaluation by US Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) across crewed and uncrewed systems in air, land, and maritime domains.

The cells were purchased by non-profit innovation hub SOFWERX in partnership with USSOCOM and, while modest in scale, the sale represents early commercial validation of Li-S Energy’s technology and a funded commitment to evaluate its performance benefits.

The first delivery supports an early-stage evaluation to identify alignment with prospective special operations use cases, and a positive outcome could position the company to supply further cell batches tailored to specific platforms and mission domains.

While any commercial outcome would depend on those results and on subsequent procurement decisions, Li-S managing director Dr Lee Finniear said the potential opportunity across USSOCOM and the broader US defence market could be substantial.

USSOCOM oversees the US military’s special operations forces and its missions are among the hardest in defence, often carried out in contested and remote environments far from re-supply, where endurance, weight, and reliability can determine mission success.

The agency is rapidly deploying uncrewed and autonomous systems in every domain from aerial systems (micro-drones to long-endurance platforms) and ground robots to uncrewed surface and sub-surface vessels.
Energy density and weight are critical to the performance of each of these platforms, with the goal of greater range, longer endurance, and increased payload.
Li-S Energy’s lithium-sulphur cells, which lack the graphite, nickel, or cobalt content of conventional lithium-ion batteries, offer significant capability enhancements beyond a drone’s own systems.

SOFWERX operates under a long-term partnership intermediary agreement with USSOCOM to fast-track promising technology into defence operations by hosting evaluations outside of the traditional procurement system, giving companies a direct route to USSOCOM without the full complexity of a conventional government contracting framework.
For Li-S Energy, that means cells are assessed quickly on their technical merits by the people closest to the operational requirement.
SOFWERX chief technology officer Brian Andrews referred to energy as being one of the hardest constraints as the USSOCOM operates “at the very edge of what technology allows”.
“As platforms become smaller, more autonomous, and more widely distributed across air, land and sea, the demand for batteries that deliver more energy at less weight only grows,” he said.

“We are continually searching for advanced energy sources that can extend endurance, range and payload, and we look forward to evaluating Li-S Energy’s lithium-sulphur cells—if the technology delivers on its promise, advances like this could translate directly into greater reach and capability for the warfighter.”

title: Li-S Energy Completes First Commercial Sale of Lithium-Sulphur Cells for US Military Evaluation
